source_location: Source: web page, section 'Family Guide & Frequently Asked Questions'
quotation: Based on current district requirements and practices, student information entered into approved tools must remain within the Broward County Public Schools environment; student information is not used to train district-approved Artificial Intelligence models.

Foundational model vendors must ensure that stakeholder information, copyrighted material, or proprietary CPS intellectual property is not used to train their models without explicit permission. Application layer vendors must ensure that the same is not used in the fine-tuning of their tools or shared with the foundational model vendor without explicit permission.
Information input into GenAI tools that have not been approved by the District may be used for algorithm training and made available to other users of the system outside the district.
Student data stays protected — Approved enterprise AI tools do not use OCPS data to train public AI models, and sensitive information may only be entered into tools approved for that type of data.
The vetting process shall include a review of the tool’s privacy policy, data storage practices, training and data policies, and compliance with FERPA.
Vendors may not use district data to train AI models unless explicitly authorized by the district.

source_location: Source: web page, section 'AI for Staff'
quotation: Entering PII into generative AI tools should always be avoided, as this information is often stored on the tool’s servers and used to train the AI model. This poses risks of violating privacy regulations like FERPA, creating legal consequences, and damaging trust. Only district approved AI tools, like Gemini, should be used.

No AI system shall collect, store, or transmit PII without prior approval through the Division’s vetting process and a signed Data Privacy Agreement that defines permissible uses, retention limits, and security standards.
The vendor provides clear data usage and retention policies.

Google Gemini and Adobe Express with Firefly were selected because they meet needed cybersecurity and privacy requirements and each vendor has an executed contract with the School District.
